transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Donna, an AI assistant calling for Alex at Acme. This call is recorded. I saw your Redis rate limiter. Got a few minutes for a quick screen?
Your README says it handles 50k requests a second. How did you measure that, and what broke first?

I load tested with k6 against a single Redis node. The first thing that broke was the Lua script, because I was doing a sorted set trim on every call, so p99 jumped. I moved to a fixed window with a token bucket fallback and it went from about 12k to 50k.
Nice. On the payments team, what went wrong with idempotency keys?
Honestly I mostly read the code. I think there was some issue with retries but I wasn't really on that part.
Fair enough. What's one thing you'd want to own in your first two weeks?

The API gateway. I'd want to put real rate limiting and tracing in front of it, because that's where I've actually built stuff, and I'd write down what I find in the first week before changing anything.
Thanks Sam, I'll pass my notes to Alex.
